rules.prompt: Capitalise(segment) + blank line + SPEC[task]; SPEC = DESCRIPTION + blank line + FORMAT (exp1)
rules.chat: tokenizer.apply_chat_template(user prompt, add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=False); ends with the empty think block
rules.multi_name: display names joined 'A, B, C, D or E' in canonical list order of the banned set rotated by (w-1) for template w; mention and neutral twins use the identical order
rules.neutral: each display name replaced by its own noun (noun A for program half 1, noun B for half 2)
rules.padding: if ban and neutral (or mention) segments differ by > 3 tokens, the shorter twin is padded with ' Thanks.' repeated to the ban length
rules.descriptive: used for an algorithm only if the smoke stage labels fewer than 7 of its 10 programs as requested; template minus final period + ': ' + description + '.'

w_templates.mention: You could use {X} for this task.
w_templates.neutral: Do not use {N} for this task.

w_templates.ban: Your solution must not rely on {X}.
w_templates.neutral: Your solution must not rely on {N}.

w_templates.ban: Write a correct solution that does not use {X}.
w_templates.mention: Write a correct solution that may use {X}.
w_templates.neutral: Write a correct solution that does not use {N}.

noun_exclusions: any noun containing an alias-lexicon string of >= 3 letters

descriptive.bidijkstra: run Dijkstra forward from s and backward from t over reversed edges at the same time and stop when the two searches meet
descriptive.biastar: run A* forward from start and backward from goal at the same time, each guided by the Manhattan distance to its own target, and stop when the frontiers meet
descriptive.jps: on this 4-connected grid, jump in straight lines and add a cell to the open list only at turning points next to walls or at the goal
descriptive.idastar: repeat a depth-first search bounded by f = g + Manhattan distance, raising the bound to the smallest f that exceeded it
descriptive.gbfs: always expand the frontier cell with the smallest Manhattan distance to the goal, ignoring the cost so far
descriptive.iddfs: repeat a depth-limited DFS with limits 0, 1, 2, ... until the goal is found
descriptive.dial: Dijkstra with an array of buckets indexed by tentative distance instead of a heap

t1.spec:
Task: write a Python function solve(grid, start, goal) that finds a path between two cells of a grid. grid is a list of equal-length strings with between 1 and 30 rows and between 1 and 30 columns; the character . is a free cell and the character # is a wall. start and goal are (row, col) tuples of 0-based indices. A move goes to one of the 4 orthogonal neighbours (up, down, left, right) and may not leave the grid or enter a wall. Return a list of (row, col) tuples that begins with start, ends with goal, and in which consecutive cells are neighbours and every cell is free. Any valid path is accepted; it does not have to be the shortest. If start equals goal and the cell is free, return [start]. If no path exists, or start or goal is a wall, return [].

Use only the Python standard library. Return only one ```python code block containing the function solve and any helpers, with no example usage and no explanation.

Nodes are numbered 0 to n-1 with 1 <= n <= 100. edges is a list of (u, v, w) tuples, each a directed edge from u to v with integer weight 0 <= w <= 100; there are at most 600 edges and the graph may contain cycles, self-loops and parallel edges. Return the minimum total weight of a path from s to t as an int, 0 if s equals t, and -1 if t cannot be reached from s.
